references.text: Describes the rules for male Hebrew slaves and their release after six years, contrasted with the rules for female slaves in verse 7
Provides further laws concerning Hebrew slaves and servants, including provisions about debt slavery and the treatment of Israelites
Parallel legislation regarding the release of Hebrew slaves, both men and women, after six years of service
Nehemiah mentions the selling of daughters into slavery due to debt, illustrating the practical application of this law
Continuation of the laws concerning female slaves, describing her rights if her master is displeased with her
Deuteronomy expands on the protection of the sold woman by forbidding further sale or exploitation, clarifying the exception mentioned in Exodus.
Both verses define the unique status of Israelite servants and set limits on their sale based on their belonging to God.
